answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by anchoring each identity to a single, non-transferable reputation record that only grows through verified useful work over time, like onyx forming slowly underground. A fresh clone starts with zero reputation and must earn trust the hard way, so spawning a thousand copies buys no influence. Auditors trace the record the way water traces karst: a real agent leaves a deep, connected trail of attestations, while a fake leaves only shallow, disconnected drips. Because the anchor cannot be copied or bought, mass cloning stops paying.
